h1: The Quarter Ladprao by UHG — the 4-star hotel steps from MRT Phahon Yothin that over-delivers for its price
intro: Ha Yaek Lat Phrao — the landmark five-way intersection where Lat Phrao Road meets Phahon Yothin — may not be the first neighbourhood that comes to mind for a Bangkok stay, but for travellers who want genuine transport convenience without paying luxury prices, it is hard to beat · The Quarter Ladprao by UHG sits at 80 Soi Ladprao 4, a 50-metre walk from MRT Phahon Yothin Exit 1 — directly opposite Union Mall and a short Grab from Central Plaza Ladprao · the hotel opened in 2018, has 194 rooms across multiple categories, an outdoor rooftop pool, a gym, restaurant Hilly's, and a free breakfast buffet included in most packages · rates start from approximately THB 1,400 per night for a standard room, rising in peak periods · Trip.com score: 9.1 out of 10 from 1,880 verified guest reviews.

body.html: Why the location matters so much here — the single most important thing about The Quarter Ladprao by UHG is where it stands. MRT Phahon Yothin Exit 1 is 50 metres from the hotel entrance — you walk out of the lobby, turn towards the station and you are there. No crossing a busy road, no motorcycle taxi, no Grab. From Phahon Yothin station you can ride the Blue Line to Chatuchak Park, Huai Khwang, Phetchaburi, Si Lom and interchange points with the BTS Skytrain without touching street traffic. For a Bangkok hotel below the luxury price tier, this is a genuinely rare combination. At street level there is a 7-Eleven right at the hotel entrance — mentioned in dozens of guest reviews as an underrated convenience for late arrivals, early departures, or anyone who needs bottled water and snacks without searching. Union Mall is directly across the road. Central Plaza Ladprao, one of Bangkok's largest shopping centres with the Phahon Yothin–BTS Ha Yaek Lat Phrao interchange above it, is under 10 minutes on foot.

Rooms, design and what real guests say — the hotel's 194 rooms span several categories: Studio King (entry-level), Superior King Room (24 m², floors 9–16, king bed), Deluxe Twin Room (29 m², floors 9–16, two singles) and Family Room (queen plus two singles). All rooms include air-conditioning, a 49-inch Smart TV, a minibar fridge, a safe, complimentary bottled water and free Wi-Fi. From 1,880 reviews on Trip.com the scores that stand out are Location 9.4 and Cleanliness 9.2, with Service (9.0) and Amenities (9.0) close behind. The recurring praise in written reviews: clean, well-maintained rooms; a fast and smooth check-in experience; genuinely attentive staff. The recurring caveat: the room design in some units feels dated — this is a 2018 property that has been running hard, and the 2025–2026 renovation programme is addressing it room by room. A small number of extended-stay reviews mention a minor ant issue; a handful report occasional TV signal interruptions. Both appear isolated rather than systemic.

"Walked out of MRT Exit 1 and the hotel was right there — I was in my room within five minutes of arriving at the station. For Bangkok that is remarkable. The pool on the 6th floor was quiet, the breakfast had more variety than I expected, and the staff were warm and helpful throughout."

Pool, gym and facilities — the rooftop pool on the 6th floor is described in guest photos and reviews as genuinely pleasant, not the cramped afterthought you find on some urban hotels in this price bracket. The surrounding terrace gets good afternoon sun and the view takes in the Lat Phrao Road corridor. The Urban Fit gym is a properly equipped fitness centre, not a token treadmill-and-bench setup; there is also a steam room for recovery. Restaurant Hilly's serves Thai and international cuisine; the breakfast buffet covers the expected spread of hot Thai dishes (rotating daily), fresh fruit, baked items and international options. Multiple reviews rate it as good value for the price. The hotel also has a café, a bar/lounge, a business centre and 24-hour room service.

Breakfast, staff and ratings across platforms — the breakfast at Hilly's receives consistent positive mentions on both Trip.com and TripAdvisor, with guests noting the daily-changing Thai options and the quality of the fresh fruit. Staff fluency in English is highlighted frequently in international reviews, with guests describing the team as proactive rather than reactive — a distinction that matters when you are navigating an unfamiliar city. TripAdvisor rates the hotel 4.9 out of 5 from 1,402 reviews and awarded it Travelers' Choice 2026, ranking it #79 of 1,384 Bangkok hotels. Agoda's aggregate score sits at 9.0. Booking.com scores the property at 8.6. Across 6,100+ aggregated guest ratings tracked by KAYAK, the hotel holds 8.9. This degree of consistency across platforms is unusual and suggests the core experience — location, cleanliness, service, breakfast — holds up across different travel styles.

Price and value — Studio King and Superior King rooms start from approximately THB 1,400–1,800 per night in low-to-mid season; KAYAK has recorded prices as low as $34 (~THB 1,150) during softer periods. Peak periods and long weekends push rates towards THB 2,500+. For a Bangkok 4-star that bundles a rooftop pool, gym, free breakfast and an MRT-adjacent address in a single rate, the value equation is strong. Parking is available but is not free, which matters for guests arriving by car from the provinces — this is worth knowing before you book.

The honest verdict — The Quarter Ladprao by UHG is the most transport-connected 4-star hotel on the Lat Phrao corridor, and that single fact anchors the whole stay. Add a working rooftop pool, a genuine breakfast buffet, well-regarded staff and a 9.1 score from nearly 2,000 guests, and the case for booking it is clear. The honest caveat is that some rooms have not yet been refreshed by the 2025–2026 renovation; post-renovation rooms are noticeably newer in feel. Ask at check-in for a recently renovated room if the condition of the interiors matters to you. If you need free parking, factor in the surcharge. If you are looking for a hotel with character or a boutique design, this is functional-modern rather than atmospheric. But as a base from which to move freely around Bangkok by MRT, at a price that does not require you to justify the expense, The Quarter Ladprao by UHG is a very easy recommendation.

highlights.title: MRT Phahon Yothin Exit 1 — 50 metres
highlights.text: Walk out of the lobby and you are at the MRT in under a minute. No street crossing, no taxi needed — genuinely rare for a Bangkok hotel at this price point.

highlights.title: Panoramic Rooftop Pool + Gym
highlights.text: 6th-floor outdoor pool, Urban Fit gym and steam room — a fuller facilities package than most comparable-price Bangkok hotels, and the pool does not disappoint in person.

highlights.title: Free Breakfast Buffet (most packages)
highlights.text: Thai hot dishes rotate daily, alongside fresh fruit, baked goods and international options. Consistently praised across platforms for variety and quality at this price tier.

honestSummary: The Quarter Ladprao by UHG offers the most convenient MRT-connected 4-star stay on the Lat Phrao corridor — 50 m from the station, with a rooftop pool, gym, free breakfast and staff that genuinely earns its 9.1 score. The only honest caveat is that the room renovation programme is ongoing; ask for a recently refreshed room at check-in.
honestChecks: If you are arriving by car and need free parking — The Quarter Ladprao has parking, but it is charged, not complimentary. Factor in the daily fee or consider another property in the area if free parking is a must.

If you are travelling during peak season or a Thai public holiday — rates can climb well above the THB 1,400 base. Book in advance with free cancellation to lock in better pricing and keep flexibility if plans change.

If room condition is important to you — some floors have been renovated post-2025, others have not yet. The difference is noticeable. At check-in, simply ask for a recently renovated room on a higher floor for the best experience.

tips.title: Take MRT Phahon Yothin Exit 1
tips.body: Exit 1 at MRT Phahon Yothin station brings you out directly facing the hotel — it is a 50-metre walk. No need to orientate yourself; the hotel sign is visible immediately.

tips.title: Use the pool early morning
tips.body: The 6th-floor rooftop pool is at its quietest between 7:00 and 9:00 — before the main breakfast rush. Good light, no crowds, and you are back for the buffet before it peaks.

tips.title: Request a high-floor renovated room
tips.body: Superior King rooms on floors 9–16 offer better views and less street noise. Ask at check-in whether the room has been recently renovated — staff are generally happy to assist if availability allows.

tips.title: 7-Eleven is open 24 hours at the entrance
tips.body: Drinks, snacks, basic medications, phone chargers and convenience items are all available next to the lobby at any hour — useful if you check in late or need to leave before breakfast opens.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — The Quarter Ladprao by UHG

faq.q: How far is The Quarter Ladprao by UHG from the MRT?
faq.a: The hotel is at 80 Soi Ladprao 4, 50 metres from MRT Phahon Yothin Exit 1. Walk out of the hotel entrance, turn towards the station and you are there in under a minute — no road crossing required. It is the closest hotel to any MRT station in the Lat Phrao corridor.

faq.q: What does The Quarter Ladprao by UHG cost per night?
faq.a: Studio King and Superior King rooms start from approximately THB 1,400–1,600 per night in standard periods. Deluxe Twin is around THB 1,800, Family Room around THB 2,200. Prices rise during Thai public holidays and peak season. Compare across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com before booking — prices vary meaningfully by platform.

faq.q: Does The Quarter Ladprao by UHG have a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes — the hotel has a Panoramic Rooftop Pool on the 6th floor (outdoor, saltwater). Views take in the Lat Phrao Road skyline. The pool is least crowded in the early morning before 9:00. There is also an Urban Fit gym and a steam room.

faq.q: Is breakfast included at The Quarter Ladprao by UHG?
faq.a: Breakfast inclusion depends on the package you book. Most packages include the free breakfast buffet at restaurant Hilly's, which offers rotating Thai hot dishes, fresh fruit, baked goods and international options. Verify at the time of booking whether your selected rate includes breakfast.

faq.q: Who is The Quarter Ladprao by UHG best suited to?
faq.a: The hotel suits business travellers, independent tourists and transit passengers who want reliable 4-star comfort with easy MRT access into central Bangkok. Its position at Ha Yaek Lat Phrao puts it within one or two MRT stops of Chatuchak, and a straightforward Blue Line ride from the Silom and Sukhumvit interchange zones.
